review_notes: Read the whole target file (22 lines, one theorem `common_subsequence_compose`, lines 8-18) and its only dependency `OAI/Combinatorics/BinaryEdit/LCSCore.lean` (`common_sublist_lower_bound`, lines 12-44; `sublist_survives_deletions`, lines 46-53), the lcs analogue `OAI/Combinatorics/BinaryEdit/LCS.lean` `lcs_overlap` (lines 74-82), and the single consumer `OAI/Combinatorics/BinaryEdit/EditLCSLower.lean` (`EditScript.common_subsequence`, lines 35-45), plus `Model.lean`/`EditDeficit.lean` for the definitions of `deficit`, `lcs` and `ed`. Generality checks: the statement is already fully polymorphic in the alphabet (`{α : Type*}`) and in the ℕ-valued costs `m n`, and it makes no structural assumption beyond `List.Sublist`; the proof (`by omega` on `u.length + v.length ≤ y.length + w.length`) needs exactly the coefficient 2, since with `k * u.length` the intermediate length `y.length` cancels only when `k = 2` (concretely `x = z = [a]`, `y = [a]`, `m = n = 0` forces `2 ≤ k`), so replacing `2` by a parameter would be either false or artificially weakened; this is why the parallel `lcs_overlap` and `EditScript.common_subsequence` in the same development also fix the coefficient `2`. Degenerate cases (`y = []`, hence `u = v = w = []`; `α` empty) are handled by the current hypotheses and conclusion. Real-valued or ℤ-valued costs would only add casts with no gain. The one abstraction the file deliberately avoids — expressing the hypothesis via `lcs` — is a design choice to keep this core independent of the `lcs` supremum (it is the `Sublist`-based counterpart of `lcs_overlap`), not a case of an overly concrete scalar type or an unnecessarily strong structural assumption. I was therefore unable to justify a finding under this rubric; remaining uncertainty is only whether a named predicate bundling the existential could be desired, which would be a refactor rather than a generalisation and is outside this rubric's scope.
